title: DuoAttention: Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference with Retrieval and Streaming Heads
one_line_claim: Differentiates attention heads into retrieval heads (requiring full KV cache) and streaming heads (constant-length cache) to reduce memory and speedup long-context inference.
method_summary: Uses a lightweight optimization-based algorithm with synthetic data to identify which attention heads need full KV-cache retention versus which can operate with constant-length caches. Retrieval heads maintain full context for long-range dependencies; streaming heads focus on recent tokens and attention sinks.

key_findings.finding: Memory reduction up to 2.55x for MHA models and 1.67x for grouped-query attention.
key_findings.quote: Memory reduction up to 2.55x for Multi-Head Attention models... and 1.67x for grouped-query attention (GQA)

key_findings.finding: Decoding speedup up to 2.18x for MHA and 1.50x for GQA.
Enables Llama-3-8B decoding with 3.3 million context length on a single A100 GPU.
key_findings.quote: enables Llama-3-8B decoding with 3.3 million context length on a single A100 GPU

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV-cache compression as a critical challenge in long-context LLM inference and focus on efficiency gains during inference.
differs_on: DuoAttention architects the compressor itself (head-level differentiation); HERALD treats the compressor as a black box and monitors for failure signals at runtime.
DuoAttention optimizes KV cache at design time; HERALD predicts and prevents failures after compression is applied.
DuoAttention uses architectural head selection; HERALD uses per-token logit features for hazard detection.
